This article compares the types of re-operations performed on patients with Inflammatory Bowel Disease (IBD), tracked under [[indikator-6|Indikator 6]]. The data highlights the specific surgical procedures required when initial interventions need revision, complication management, or further investigation.

The most frequent re-operations are diagnostic and exploratory in nature. Exploratory laparotomy (KJAH00) leads the list with 27 cases, accounting for 27.6% of the total [^src1]. Laparoscopy (KJAH01) is the second most common procedure, with 20 cases representing 20.4% [^src1]. Together, these two exploratory procedures make up nearly half of all recorded re-operations, standing out as a significant outlier pattern that suggests a heavy reliance on diagnostic assessment rather than pre-planned specific resections.

Following the leaders, specific resections and repairs are notably less common. Thin bowel resection (KJFB00) and suture of wound rupture (KJWA00) both account for 8 cases each (8.2%) [^src1]. Terminal enterostomy (KJFF13) follows with 6 cases (6.1%) [^src1]. 

At the lower end of the spectrum, a large number of specialized procedures act as trailers, each representing only 1.0% of the re-operations (often indicated by a suppressed count of '#') [^src1]. These include laparoscopic suture of the small intestine (KJFA71), ileocecal resection (KJFB20), right-sided hemicolectomy (KJFB30), and various other localized bowel operations and re-operations for bleeding or infection [^src1]. 

Because the available evidence consists of a single dated section from 2024, no longitudinal trends regarding the increase or decrease of specific re-operation types can be established. Furthermore, the data does not record specific clinical targets or thresholds to evaluate whether met or missed.
